name: Malaysia
shortSummary: India and Malaysia maintain substantial trade and a large diaspora-linked people-to-people relationship, though ties saw friction in 2019-20 after Malaysian leaders publicly criticised India's Kashmir and citizenship policies.
complexity: Comments by then-PM Mahathir Mohamad on Kashmir and the Citizenship Amendment Act in 2019-20 triggered informal Indian trade friction, including reduced palm oil purchases; ties have since stabilised.

majorAreasOfCooperation.description: India is one of the largest export markets for Malaysian palm oil.
A large ethnic Indian community in Malaysia anchors strong people-to-people links.

majorChallenges.title: Political rhetoric sensitivity
majorChallenges.description: Periodic friction over Malaysian commentary on India's domestic policies affects trade sentiment.

recentDevelopments.title: Trade ties stabilize after earlier political friction
recentDevelopments.description: Bilateral trade, including palm oil purchases, continued to recover after the 2019-20 friction over political commentary.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: Shows the relationship's underlying economic ballast reasserting itself after a period of strain.

historicalEvents.title: Diplomatic Friction over Kashmir Remarks
historicalEvents.description: Malaysian PM Mahathir Mohamad's UN remarks on Kashmir prompt informal Indian trade pushback on Malaysian palm oil.
